title: One-sided stripe supersolidity from engineered non-axisymmetric dipolar interactions
abstract: A supersolid combines density order with phase coherence, and doped lattice solids ask whether added defects can become coherent without melting the ordered background. We study a soft-core Bose-Hubbard model with isotropic hopping and an engineered non-axisymmetric dipolar interaction, \(V_{ij}=V_2(x_{ij}^2-y_{ij}^2)/r_{ij}^5+W_6/r_{ij}^6\), where the sign-changing \(d_{x^2-y^2}\) component selects a fixed \((q,0)\) stripe channel and the \(W_6/r^6\) core stabilizes the short-distance attractive branch. Using sign-problem-free quantum Monte Carlo method with worm algorithm, we find that the half-filled stripe parent responds asymmetrically to doping: the hole side forms locked commensurate stripe solids with vanishing superfluid stiffness, whereas the particle side forms a stripe supersolid with finite compressibility \(κ>0\), finite superfluid stiffness \(ρ_s>0\), and enhanced double occupancy \(D\). Keeping the same off-site kernel while increasing \(U/t\) toward the hard-core limit shows that the particle-side supersolid disappears once doublon-like defects are projected out. Thus the engineered dipolar kernel selects the fixed \((q,0)\) stripe channel, while onsite softness selects the phase-coherent defect sector.
summary: The paper theoretically investigates stripe supersolidity in a Bose-Hubbard model governed by engineered non-axisymmetric dipolar interactions. It demonstrates that the system's response to doping is highly asymmetric: particle doping stabilizes a true supersolid phase with finite superfluidity, whereas hole doping leads to locked, less coherent states. This behavior hinges critically on the presence of soft-core doublon fluctuations enabled by onsite interaction $U$.
main_problem: The study investigates whether doping defects (vacancies/interstitials) can become phase coherent without melting the ordered background in a supersolid state, and how this coherence depends on particle vs. hole doping.
main_result: The system exhibits an asymmetry: particle doping leads to a stripe supersolid with finite superfluid stiffness ($ho_s>0$) and compressibility ($\kappa>0$), while hole doping results in locked commensurate solids with vanishing $ho_s$.
method: Path-integral Quantum Monte Carlo method utilizing the worm algorithm for simulations.
model_or_system: A soft-core Bose-Hubbard model on a square lattice featuring an engineered non-axisymmetric dipolar interaction ($V_{ij} \propto (x^2-y^2)/r^5 + 1/r^6$).
key_observables: Compressibility ($\kappa$), Superfluid Stiffness ($ho_s$), Double Occupancy ($D$), and the structure factor $S(q)$ to confirm $(q,0)$ stripe order.
important_parameters: The ratio $U/t$ (controlling onsite softness) and the doping level $\delta n = n - 1/2$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the off-site dipolar kernel selects a fixed $(q,0)$ stripe channel, while the finite onsite interaction ($U$) controls defect mobility.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the asymmetric phase diagram in doping space ($\delta n$), showing plateaus on the hole side versus continuous supersolid formation on the particle side. Tables summarize how this DSS state vanishes when the soft-core doublon channel is suppressed by increasing $U/t$ towards the hard-core limit.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the Bose-Hubbard model, first establishing the role of the engineered dipolar interaction in selecting stripe order. It then compares the physical response to particle vs. hole doping, using $ho_s$, $\kappa$, and $D$ as diagnostics to prove the one-sided nature of the supersolid phase.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for realizing and controlling exotic quantum phases like stripe supersolids in controllable lattice systems, directly relevant to cold atom simulations using dipolar interactions.

(b) The momentum- space off-site kernel, eVoff(q), has a low axial (q, 0) channel, while onsite U does not choose the ordering direction. In (b), colors show the relative value of eVoff(q) after subtracting its Brillouin-zone average; the low axial region marks the selected (q, 0) channel.

FIG. 2. Fixed-shape phase diagram. Phase assignments in the (δn, η) plane, with δn = n −1/2, η = V2/t, and fixed ratios U/V2 = 30/7, W6/V2 = 3/7. Small gray dots denote simulated points; colored points and domains summarize the identified phases: superfluid (SF), mobile stripe (MS), locked stripe solid (LSS), half-filled stripe solid (HSS), and doped stripe supersolid (DSS). The HSS forms the central parent at δn = 0.
